clue.text: Ringing about a boy worker

parts.note: RE is a Latin-derived word for about or concerning
a boy is a son
the ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: Someone is calling about a lad who works somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A resounding, echoing tone is the sense shared by both words.

clue.text: Some soldiers give up and retreat

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to cede is to surrender or give up

explanation.surface: Troops surrender and fall back.
explanation.definitionFit: To move back or withdraw is to pull away.

clue.text: Roman philosopher creating a scene

indicators.note: creating suggests making a new arrangement from the letters of a scene

explanation.surface: An ancient thinker causes a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creating a scene' looks like making a fuss; 'creating' is the signal rearranging A SCENE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stoic thinker and tutor to Nero, famous from ancient Rome.

clue.text: A woman left — typical!

parts.note: Norma is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone sighs that a woman has gone, as usual.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual and standard, conforming to the expected pattern.

clue.text: A diet now in use over the whole of the country

definitions.text: over the whole of the country

indicators.note: use, in the sense of being put to work, means the letters of a diet now in are reworked

explanation.surface: A diet in vogue throughout the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'use' rearranges the letters of 'A diet now in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Extending across all parts of a nation is national in scope.

clue.text: Share out the lot

explanation.surface: Divide up everything there is.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide and distribute is one sense, and an auction batch of goods is the other.

clue.text: Expressing approbation at finding everyone Conservative?

parts.note: all means everyone
the right is the conservative side of politics

explanation.surface: Approval at discovering the whole party is Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation saying something is satisfactory or acceptable.

clue.text: Applaud artifice and bombast

parts.note: to clap is to applaud
a trap is a trick or piece of artifice

explanation.surface: Praising cunning and empty talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretentious, empty language is nonsense meant to win applause.

clue.text: Erudite people in conversation-polite, rational, earnest

indicators.note: in conversation means the letters sit inside the spoken words polite, rational, earnest

explanation.surface: Learned folk chat in a courteous, reasoned and serious way.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarly intellectuals interested in literature form a learned class.

clue.text: Cold, over-tired — in a sorry state indeed!

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
over in the sense of concerning, as on means about
tired as in hackneyed, stale and overused

explanation.surface: Someone cold and exhausted is in a wretched condition.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'over-tired' joins two separate pieces: ON (concerning) and TRITE (hackneyed).
explanation.definitionFit: A penitent person feels sorry, full of remorse for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Paint maybe about fifty, which should be manageable

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the fifty
maybe suggests the word paint could be arranged in some other order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A tin of paint around fifty pounds should be easy to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges PAINT to PIANT, and 'about' has those letters go around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flexible and easily bent or influenced is easy to handle.

clue.text: The man who is never overruled

definitions.text: The man who is never overruled

parts.words: The man who is never overruled
parts.note: reads like a strong-willed person in an argument, but describes an absolute ruler whom nobody can overrule

explanation.surface: Someone who always gets their way in a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocrat holds total power, so no authority can overturn any decision.

clue.text: A skilled technician is less likely to feel fatigue

explanation.surface: A trained engineer is less prone to tiredness.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanic who assembles machinery is one sense; in better physical shape is the comparative of healthy.

clue.text: Walker is anything but imaginative

explanation.surface: A rambler is decidedly unimaginative.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on foot is one sense; dull and uninspired is the other.

clue.text: Water these, otherwise they'll be dear

indicators.note: otherwise means the words water these are taken in another order

explanation.surface: Advice on watering plants so they will not become expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges WATER THESE; 'dear' looks like costly but is a term of endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: A loved one or darling is addressed as dear.

clue.text: Socialist leader finding his greatest strength lies in oratory

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Socialist

parts.note: peaking means reaching a high point of strength

explanation.surface: A left-wing politician's main talent is public speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lies in' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Public speaking or delivery of speeches is the art of rhetoric.

clue.text: The crooked fancy forging such a note

explanation.surface: A strange whim leads to writing a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: A crotchet is originally a little hook, hence 'crooked'; 'forging' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A perverse whim or odd notion is one sense; a quarter note in music is the other.

clue.text: Safeguard the small change to save for the future

parts.note: P is a penny, the smallest change
to reserve is to keep back for later use

explanation.surface: Protecting loose coins so they can be saved.
explanation.definitionFit: To protect or keep safe from harm.

clue.text: Crests displayed by some birds

parts.note: some means a part of something
crests are ridges, as on a hill or roof

explanation.surface: Some birds show off feathered crests on their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crests' looks like plumage; it means hill ridges, set after PART.
explanation.definitionFit: Game birds of the pheasant family are a specific example of birds.

clue.text: Short story about abstemious trainee

indicators.note: about means the story goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a lie is a story or fib
TT means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A brief tale about a sober apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: Small in height or stature.

clue.text: Get through little run in a bit

indicators.note: in means the run goes inside the bit

parts.note: a piece is a bit
R is the abbreviation for run in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: Getting past a small run during a short stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: To penetrate or puncture is to go through.

clue.text: Horrified at gash made

indicators.note: made suggests something is formed anew from the letters of at gash

explanation.surface: Appalled at a wound inflicted.
explanation.definitionFit: Filled with shock and dismay.

clue.text: The person drawing a little chart is totally absorbed

indicators.note: absorbed means the letters are swallowed up inside the words chart is totally

explanation.surface: Someone sketching a small diagram is completely engrossed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbed' looks like engrossed; it hides the answer across 'chart is totally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes pictures with pencil is a painter or illustrator.

clue.text: Impressive industrial action

explanation.surface: A notable walkout by workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye-catching and remarkable is one sense; workers walking out in a dispute is the other.

clue.text: Stick popular girl next to egghead

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
her is the pronoun for a girl
the head of the word egg is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fashionable woman stays close to an intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual; it is the head, or first letter, of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be inherent or remain fixed within is to stay attached, a sense of stick.

clue.text: Carriage of state "down under"

explanation.surface: A vehicle belonging to an Australian region.
explanation.definitionFit: A light four-wheeled horse-drawn coach is one sense; an Australian state in the south-east is the other.

clue.text: Article in gutter press backing surmise

indicators.note: in means the article goes inside the other piece
backing means the word for the gutter press is read backwards

parts.note: a rag is a disreputable newspaper
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A tabloid speculates about a news item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutter press' is a single idea here: a rag, a trashy newspaper. 'backing' reverses it to GAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer or conclude from evidence is to guess or suppose.

clue.text: Profit from it-resent irregularity

indicators.note: irregularity means the letters of it-resent are put in a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: Benefit comes from resentment in an unusual way.
explanation.definitionFit: Money earned on savings or a loan is a gain or return.
